name: Medusa Spirit Charmer

alignment.name: Evil
alignment.description:
Evil creatures don’t necessarily go out of their way to hurt people, but they’re perfectly willing to take advantage of the weakness of others to acquire what they want.
	Evil creatures use rules and order to maximize personal gain. They don’t care whether laws hurt other people. They support institutional structures that give them power, even if that power comes at the expense of others’ freedom. Slavery and rigid caste structures are not only acceptable but desirable to evil creatures, as long as they are in a position to benefit from them.

description: This is the size of a typical human and serves as a standard in the game. This category has no special rules.

hit.description: poison damage, and the target takes a -2 penalty to saving throws until the end of the medusa’s next turn.
psychic damage, and the target must end its next turn 2 squares closer to or adjacent to the medusa or else take 3d6 psychic damage.
The target’s weapons and implements appear to become snakes, and the target cannot use weapon or implement powers (save ends).

powers.name: Stony Glare
powers.trigger: An enemy ends its turn within 2 squares of the medusa.

attacks.name: Attack
attacks.targets: the triggering enemy in the blast

nestedAttackDescriptions: The use of an appropriate power, such as divine cleansing.
The willing kiss of the medusa that petrified the creature (a medusa might do this to gain information or to luxuriate in the victim’s fear before returning it to stone).
The medusa responsible for the petrification is killed and its blood is applied to the stony lips of the victim before a full day passes.
